title: Monster Breeder -beta test
author: Robonotes1760
selftext:
Here is my new open source game, Monster Breeder:

Play here: [https://bridgewater-brunel.me.uk/games/monsterbreeder/](https://bridgewater-brunel.me.uk/games/monsterbreeder/)

Github: [https://github.com/jamespetts/MonsterBreeder](https://github.com/jamespetts/MonsterBreeder)

Premise: you breed monsters to protect treasure from four classes of adventurer. Breeding uses a deep, realistic genetic simulation. A campaign mode allows you to build up better, stronger monsters while dealing with easier adventurers as they will get more challenging later in the game. Designed in the style of a late 1990s/early 2000s management sim.

Development process: M365 Copilot writing Javascript to a single .html file (as it only lets me upload 3 files). No MCP, no subscription (beyond the M365 subscription), unlimited prompts, and built with GPT 5.5 and 5.6. Music: generated using [musichero.ai](http://musichero.ai) (a frontend for the Suno engine). 

I should be grateful for any beta test feedback. 

Graphics are still fairly basic as I do not think that I have discovered a reliable graphics authoring pipeline as yet.

comments.author: CertainBlue
comments.body: copilot, really? You're the first person I ever see that uses copilot for this kind of project, that's surprising. I'm not saying it's a bad thing.

replies.author: Robonotes1760
replies.body: I use it because I don't have to pay and it's unlimited usage for good GPT models.

replies.author: Conscious_Regret_140
replies.body: GPT models? What do you mean?

replies.author: Robonotes1760
replies.body: Open AI's models in the GPT 5.x series.

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body:
I tried it....

So a trend I've noticed about AI games and there onboarding is they are incredibly verbose. AI likes to talk and explain, this NOT for games.

For your tutorial onboardin, you need "Select", "Drag", "Drop", "Result".

So bring the user inthe map, have something flashing they have to click, that click lets the interact with the screen and put someting on the map. Then they see a result happen.

replies.author: Robonotes1760
replies.body: Thank you - that is interesting feedback. It is difficult to know exactly what a new player needs to know and what is obvious.

replies.author: promptling
replies.body: That uncertainty is exactly what a clean first session test can answer. Give five people the current build with no guidance and ask them to narrate what they think breeding changes, what protects treasure, and why they lost. The first repeated wrong assumption is probably the tutorial you actually need. Full disclosure, I am building [Patchloop](https://patchloop.io/) for agentically built games in progress, with focused playtest rooms and feedback tied to each version. Monster Breeder feels like a great fit for a short onboarding test if you want to share it there.

comments.author: theDawckta
comments.body: Your ui is a little unreadable. to small for my eyes. You could get a lot more readability color coding some things or iconizing some things.

replies.author: Robonotes1760
replies.body: Thank you for your feedback. Can I clarify - is it the size or colour contrast that is the issue?

replies.author: theDawckta
replies.body: Just size. Some larger color coded headers would go a long way as well. Even better if you can give things icons.
